title: The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Sanjiv Kumar Goyal And Another on 6 January, 2012

The New India Assurance Company Limited vs Sanjiv Kumar Goyal And Another on 6 January, 2012

 STATE CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION UTTARAKHAND
                         DEHRADUN

                    FIRST APPEAL NO. 178 / 2009

The New India Assurance Company Limited
having one of its Branch Office at
Bapu Ashram Palace, 29, Dehradun Road
Rishikesh, District Dehradun through
Divisional Manager, The New India Assurance Company Limited
8/6-7, Astley Hall, Dehradun
                                         ......Appellant / Opposite Party

                                Versus

1.    Sh. Sanjiv Kumar Goyal S/o Sh. Bala Prasad

2.    Smt. Rekha Goyal W/o Sh. Sanjiv Kumar Goyal
      Both R/o 104/18, Dehradun Road
      Hanumant Kripa, Rishikesh
      District Dehradun
                                      ......Respondents / Complainants

Sh. M.K. Kohli, Learned Counsel for the Appellant
Sh. Rajiv Kakkar, Learned Counsel for Respondents

Coram: Hon'ble Mr. Justice B.C. Kandpal, President
       Mr. C.C. Pant,                    Member
       Mrs. Kusum Lata Sharma,           Member

Dated: 06/01/2012

                               ORDER

(Per: Justice B.C. Kandpal, President):

This is insurer's appeal under Section 15 of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986 against the order dated 21.08.2009 passed by the District Forum, Dehradun in consumer complaint No. 176 of 2008. By the order impugned, the District Forum has allowed the consumer complaint and directed the appellant - insurance company to pay sum of Rs. 92,176/- to the respondents - complainants together with interest @7% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint till payment.
2

2. In brief the facts of the case, as stated in the consumer complaint, are that the complainant No. 1 had purchased a Family Floater Mediclaim Policy from the opposite party - The New India Assurance Company Limited for himself, his wife and his son. The policy was valid for the period from 09.04.2008 to 08.04.2009. It was alleged that in the month of July, 2008, the complainant No. 2 - Smt. Rekha Goyal had problem of dim vision in both her eyes. She went for a medical check-up. On examination, she was told that she has Cataract in both her eyes and was advised Cataract surgery. The complainant No. 2 underwent Cataract surgery on 08.07.2008 and a sum of Rs. 90,000/- was spent in the surgery. The complainants lodged a claim with the insurance company, which was repudiated by the insurance company. Alleging deficiency in service on the part of the insurance company, the complainants filed a consumer complaint before the District Forum, Dehradun.

3. The insurance company filed written statement before the District Forum and pleaded that the claim lodged was repudiated under Clause 4.3 of the policy. As per the said clause, the disease / ailment with which the complainant No. 2 suffered, was not covered for the first two years from the date of inception of the policy. Since the policy was purchased on 09.04.2008, hence the claim was not payable.

4. The District Forum, on an appreciation of the material on record, allowed the consumer complaint vide impugned order dated 21.08.2009 in the above terms. Aggrieved by the said order, the insurance company has filed this appeal.

5. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and have also perused the record.

3

6. The claim was repudiated under Clause 4.3 of the policy. The complainants have stated that they were not made aware of the terms and conditions of the policy and only the policy was handed over to them and since they were not made aware of the terms and conditions of the policy and were not provided the same by the insurance company, the claim can not be repudiated on the basis of such condition which was not supplied to them.

7. From the evidence on record, it is evident that the complainants have been taking mediclaim policies from other insurance companies for the last several years. The policy in question was purchased from The New India Assurance Company Limited on 09.04.2008. The defence of the insurance company is that since the insured - complainant No. 2 suffered from Cataract within a period of two years from the date of inception of the policy and hence the insurance company is not liable to indemnify the mediclaim expenses incurred in her treatment. The complainants have come up with a specific case that the terms and conditions of the policy were not provided to them. Learned counsel for respondents has cited a decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of M/s Modern Insulators Ltd. Vs. The Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.; 2000 (1) CPR 93 (SC). In the said case, the insured was supplied only the cover note and schedule of the policy. The claim was repudiated on the ground that the insured contravened condition in exclusion clause. It was held that the exclusion clause not included in the policy, nor disclosed to the insured and the insurance company can not claim benefit of exclusion clause. Learned counsel also cited a decision of the Hon'ble National Commission in the case of M/s National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Suman Oil Industries; 2002 NCJ 544 (NC). In the said case, the insurance company issued only a cover note and the exclusion clause 4 remained uncommunicated to the insured. It was held that the repudiation of the claim on the basis of exclusion clause, is deficiency in service.

8. Though the insurance company has adduced evidence by way of an affidavit of Sh. G.S. Gupta, Senior Divisional Manager, averring therein that the terms and conditions of the policy were supplied to the complainants, but the complainants have also averred in their affidavit that the insurance company had issued the policy cover note only and the terms and conditions were neither supplied nor disclosed to them. This appears to be believable because the policy cover note does not mention of any enclosures with it. Therefore, we arrive at a definite conclusion that the insurance company has made deficiency in service by repudiating the claim of the complainants on the basis of Clause 4.3 of the policy and the view taken by the District Forum can not be said to be justified.

9. No dispute has been raised regarding the amount of compensation awarded by the District Forum. Even otherwise, the District Forum has awarded the compensation of Rs. 92,176/- on the basis of the medical bills submitted on record by the complainants. Therefore, it can not be said that the District Forum has awarded excessive compensation. The interest awarded @7% p.a. also can not be said to be on the higher side. Thus, the appeal being devoid of merit, is liable to be dismissed.

10. For the reasons aforesaid, appeal is dismissed. No order as to costs.

(SMT. KUSUM LATA SHARMA) (C.C. PANT) (JUSTICE B.C. KANDPAL) K
